title: Affine-space composition law
statement:
In the finite-coefficient purity conventions [def-pur-conventions], put $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$. Let $Y$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme, $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$, and $d,e\geq1$. Write $p_e:\mathbf A^e_Y\to Y$, $p_d:\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^e_Y}\to\mathbf A^e_Y$, and $p_{d+e}:\mathbf A^{d+e}_Y\to Y$ for the projections [def-sbc-affine-space]. For the ordered affine-space comparisons [def-pur-affine-space-comparison], under the canonical identification $\mathbf A^{d+e}_Y\cong\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^e_Y}$ one has
$$
\gamma_{p_{d+e},K}=c_{p_e,p_d}^{-1}\circ\gamma_{p_d,Rp_e^!K}\circ Lp_d^*(\gamma_{p_e,K})(d)[2d],
$$
after the canonical reassociation of twists, shifts and pullbacks. Here $c_{g,f}:R(gf)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^!Rg^!$ is the adjunction-preserving composition isomorphism for the exceptional inverse image [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The Koszul sign interchanging the two $A(1)$-tensor factors in the product of $(d)[2d]$ and $(e)[2e]$ is $+1$, both factors being of even degree; the two orderings of the affine coordinates give the same composite comparison.

proof.text: Fix the coefficient and geometric domains. All the projections in the coordinate towers are separated of finite type between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, with their standard projective compactifications. Their bases and sources are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied to their finite-type structural maps to $\operatorname{Spec}k$: a field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and the unit ideal. The adjunction on bounded-below etale-origin inputs is [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]; [thm-sf-preservation-class] implies that each intermediate exceptional pullback of $K$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Thus every occurrence of $\gamma_{p_d,Rp_e^!K}$ is in its declared domain. Twists are locally free rank-one coefficient sheaves by [prop-weil-twist-preserves]. We may calculate compact-support morphisms on the ordinary etale site: [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] supplies etale representatives, [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] is fully faithful on $D^+$, [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison] identifies the two compact-support functors, and [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] applies to $\nu$ as well as to scheme pullbacks. The exceptional adjunction is transported by the actual Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], rather than by an unbounded pro-etale adjoint assumption. The finite Tor condition is reflected on an etale representative: tensor it with any etale module sheaf and apply the exact, fully faithful, monoidal $\nu^*$; the resulting tensor has the required cohomological vanishing, which is reflected on each cohomology sheaf by the faithful exact inverse image (faithfulness on sheaves follows from full faithfulness on complexes concentrated in degree zero). This reflection does not require applying bounded-below full faithfulness to an unbounded tensor complex. These facts identify the transposes and permit checking their equality on the etale site.

source.place: Proof, Step 1: domains of the ordered affine-line comparisons; finite-level site and adjunction interfaces

proof.text:
The finite-level twist in the preceding identification is the usual etale torsion twist at every $n$, including ramified stages. Indeed choose $r\geq1$ with $\ell^rA=0$. From [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] and clauses (2)--(3) of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], associativity of ordinary tensor gives
$$A(1)=\mathbb Z_\ell(1)\otimes_{\mathbb Z_\ell}A\cong(\mathbb Z_\ell(1)/\ell^r)\otimes_{\mathbb Z/\ell^r}A\cong\mu_{\ell^r}\otimes_{\mathbb Z/\ell^r}A.$$
These are rank-one locally free sheaves; this calculation uses no flatness of $A$ over $\mathbb Z/\ell^r$. Their powers give the same identification for the positive twists used here. It is compatible with pullback because roots of unity and all the displayed tensor constructions pull back. Thus the finite torsion trace construction with annihilator $\ell^r$ is exactly the twist convention in the affine-line comparison of [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]. No divisibility assumption on $n$ by the ramification index is introduced.

source.place: Proof, Step 1: identification of the finite coefficient Tate factors

proof.text: Obtain the coherence of $c$ from adjunctions. For $X\xrightarrow f Z\xrightarrow g Y$, use the composite adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], whose counit is $\varepsilon_g\circ Rg_!(\varepsilon_f)$. The mate of $\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gf)_!$ from [thm-sf-comp-composition] identifies its right adjoint with $Rf^!Rg^!$ and is $c_{g,f}$. Pasting along the adjunctions in clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting] shows that the two $c$-composites for three arrows are the mates of the two $\alpha$-composites. Those are equal by the associativity clause of [thm-sf-comp-composition]; the mate correspondence is a bijection, so the $c$-composites agree. When one arrow is an identity, the direct-image composition map is the identity by [thm-sf-comp-composition], and its mate is the identity of the right adjoint by clause (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-mate-pasting]; hence the corresponding $c$ is the unit identification. Pullback composition uses [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]; on constant coefficient sheaves it is termwise inverse-image composition. Tensor reassociation is that of the tensor powers defining the twists. This supplies the coherence actually needed when parentheses in the tower are changed.

source.place: Lemma 0DV0 (lemma-compose-counits), Lemma 0B65 (lemma-transformation-between-functors-and-adjoints); applied to blueprint Proof, Step 2

proof.text:
Prove the displayed composition identity by induction on the length of the first block. Abbreviate $F_f(M)=Lf^*M(a)[2a]$ for an $a$-coordinate projection. In the ordered tower [def-pur-affine-space-comparison], appending one line $u$ replaces $\Gamma_{g,K}$ by
$$c_{g,u}^{-1}\circ\gamma_{u,Rg^!K}\circ F_u(\Gamma_{g,K}),\qquad\Gamma_{\mathrm{id},K}=\mathrm{id}_K.$$
The assertion for a first block of length one is exactly this recursion. Suppose it holds for a first block $f$ of length $a$, and append $u$. Substitute $\Gamma_{gf,K}=c_{g,f}^{-1}\gamma_{f,Rg^!K}F_f(\Gamma_{g,K})$ into the recursion. Naturality of $\gamma_u$ moves $F_u(c_{g,f}^{-1})$ across $\gamma_u$. Here naturality follows directly by transposing the natural projection-formula composite in [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison], with the natural projection map of [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. The resulting two consecutive $c^{-1}$ maps equal the reassociated ones by Step 3. The remaining factors $\gamma_u F_u(\gamma_f)$ are precisely $\gamma_{fu}$ at $Rg^!K$. This proves the induction step. Taking the two block lengths to be $d,e$ gives exactly the equality in the statement, with source $Lp_{d+e}^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]$ and target $Rp_{d+e}^!K$. This argument concerns regrouping a fixed ordered list; coordinate interchange is established separately below.

source.place: Proof, Steps 1--2: induction spelling out the reassociation of the ordered tower

proof.text:
Let $L_Y=\mathbf A^1_Y$, $a:L_Y\to Y$, $T=A_{L_Y}(1)[2]$, $U=Ra_!T$, and $t:U\to A_Y$ the line integration of [def-pur-affine-line-purity-comparison]. It is compatible with change of base. To check the specific map, use its defining compactification $a=qj$, and put $\bar T=A_{\mathbf P^1_Y}(1)[2]$, so $j^*\bar T=T$: the trace $t_q$ and its normalized counit commute with base change by [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], applied with annihilator $\ell^r$ from Step 2. The open-extension comparison is [lem-weil-pbc-etale-shriek-base-change-modules], and the compact-support exchange and its pasting are [thm-cbc-finite-torsion]. Applying these to the open-adjunction counit followed by the projective trace, $Rq_*j_!j^*\bar T\to Rq_*\bar T\xrightarrow{t_q}A_Y$ yields, for a morphism $v:Y'\to Y$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes (hence between Noetherian schemes), the equality
$$v^*t=t'\circ\operatorname{Ex}_!:\ v^*Ra_!T\longrightarrow A_{Y'}.$$
The module open-extension comparison is applied termwise here; $T$ is a shifted locally free sheaf and inverse image and extension by zero are exact. The transport of Step 1 gives the identical equality at the finite pro-etale stage. In particular every line trace in a product tower is the pullback of this one $t$.

source.place: Proof, Steps 3--4: base-change identity for the line trace needed to compare the two coordinate towers

proof.text:
Write $X_m=L_Y^{\times_Ym}=\mathbf A^m_Y$, $T_m=A_{X_m}(m)[2m]$, $F_mK=p_m^*K\otimes^LT_m$, and let $\tau_{m,K}:Rp_{m!}F_mK\to K$ be the exceptional transpose of the ordered $\Gamma_{m,K}$. Put $I_m=\tau_{m,A_Y}$; these are temporary morphisms in this proof. For a tower $f,g$, the composite-adjunction formula of Step 3 says that the transpose of $c_{g,f}^{-1}\gamma_{f,Rg^!K}F_f(\Gamma_{g,K})$ is
$$\varepsilon_{g,K}\circ Rg_!(\varepsilon_{f,Rg^!K})\circ Rg_!Rf_!\bigl(\gamma_{f,Rg^!K}\circ F_f(\Gamma_{g,K})\bigr).$$
Combining the middle two factors first gives $Rg_!\tau_{f,Rg^!K}\circ Rg_!Rf_!F_f(\Gamma_{g,K})$. Naturality of $\tau_f$ changes this to $Rg_!(\Gamma_{g,K})\circ Rg_!(\tau_{f,F_gK})$. The full transpose is therefore
$$\tau_{g,K}\circ Rg_!(\tau_{f,F_gK}).$$
For a line, its definition is $\tau_{1,K}=(1_K\otimes t)\circ\mathrm{PF}^{-1}$. Induction using this pasted formula and the composition pentagon and naturality of [prop-sf-pf-coherence] now gives
$$\tau_{m,K}=(1_K\otimes I_m)\circ\mathrm{PF}_{p_m}^{-1}:Rp_{m!}(p_m^*K\otimes^LT_m)\longrightarrow K.$$
Specifically, two successive inverse projection maps identify the pasted source with $K\otimes Rp_{m!}T_m$ by that pentagon; naturality moves $1_K$ past the inner trace, leaving the very same pasted map evaluated at $K=A_Y$, namely $I_m$. This proves the asserted formula and does not assume any coordinate invariance.

source.place: Proof, Steps 2--4: explicit counit calculation reducing equality of comparisons to equality of integration maps

proof.text:
Use the compact-support relative product [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] with the $m$ copies of $(a:L_Y\to Y,T)$. Denote its iterated isomorphism by $\kappa_m:Rp_{m!}T_m\xrightarrow{\sim}U^{\otimes^Lm}$. Only (A2), (A3), (A4) of [def-sf-datum] are involved: their concrete finite-level inputs are respectively [thm-cbc-finite-torsion], [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula], and [thm-sf-comp-composition]. The objects on the source factors are shifted locally free rank-one sheaves, so meet the finite-Tor and constructibility conditions. One further condition must be checked: the second projection formula in the binary relative product uses $V_m=Rp_{m!}T_m$ as its base coefficient. For $m=1$, apply [lem-amb-affine-space-top-trace] with $S=Y$, $d=1$ and $N=\ell^r$ chosen in Step 2. Its finite commutative coefficient ring is $A=A_{E,n}$, with $NA=0$; $N$ is invertible on the $k$-scheme $Y$ since $\ell\ne p$, and $Y$ is Noetherian by Step 1. The input $A_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]$ is bounded below. The cited statement identifies the source of its counit with $Ra_!A_{\mathbf A^1_Y}(1)[2]$ and says the counit is an isomorphism. Used only in dimension one, it therefore gives an isomorphism of objects $U\cong A_Y$ on the ordinary etale site; Step 2 identifies its ordinary finite Tate sheaf $\mu_N\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A$ with $T[-2]$, and Step 1 realizes it pro-etale. Thus $U$ is bounded constructible of Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. Inductively suppose $V_m$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. The binary relative product on $(p_m,T_m)$ and $(a,T)$ then uses projection formulas only with finite-Tor coefficients $T$ (pulled back to the inner base) and $V_m$ on $Y$. Its concrete hypotheses are supplied by the three finite-level inputs just cited, so it gives $V_{m+1}\cong V_m\otimes^LU$, which is again bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude since $U\cong A_Y$. In particular the object induction gives $V_m\cong A_Y$ and Tor amplitude $[0,0]$ for every $m\geq1$: the base is $V_1=U\cong A_Y$, and $V_{m+1}\cong V_m\otimes^LU\cong A_Y\otimes_A^LA_Y\cong A_Y$. The tensor-unit equalities are elementary. This proves the required domain condition at every stage, independently of any identification of the ordered maps $I_m$ with the top-trace counits. Thus this use imposes neither a duality axiom nor a general ambient pro-etale adjoint assumption. The definition of the binary product map in [thm-sf-kunneth-relative] identifies the successive projection maps and exchanges in Step 6 with $\kappa_{m+1}$. More explicitly the inner line trace, after exchange, is $1\otimes t$ by Step 5; the outer integration is $I_m$. Hence
$$I_1=t,\qquad I_{m+1}=(I_m\otimes t)\circ\kappa_{m,1},\qquad I_m=t^{\otimes m}\circ\kappa_m,$$
where $\kappa_{m,1}$ has target $(Rp_{m!}T_m)\otimes U$ and tensor units in $A_Y^{\otimes m}$ are suppressed. The triple-product and projection-formula clauses of [lem-sf-kunneth-coherence] identify every parenthesization with this same $\kappa_m$. This is a calculation of the integration map, not an appeal to a purity or supported Kunneth theorem.

source.place: Proof, Steps 3--4: identifying coordinate interchange with tensor interchange using the relative compact-support product

proof.text:
For an adjacent transposition of the $m$ line factors, the symmetry clause of [lem-sf-kunneth-coherence] identifies the induced map on $Rp_{m!}T_m$ with the corresponding symmetry of $U^{\otimes m}$. Tensor naturality gives
$$(t\otimes t)\circ\sigma_{U,U}=\sigma_{A_Y,A_Y}\circ(t\otimes t)=t\otimes t,$$
since the symmetry of two tensor units is the identity. On the source, the tensor sign symmetry of [def-kun-derived-tensor] is $x\otimes y\mapsto(-1)^{ij}y\otimes x$; for $T=A(1)[2]$ the two degrees are $-2,-2$, so the sign is $+1$. Locally choose a generator $b$ of the rank-one twist [prop-weil-twist-preserves]; the unshifted interchange sends $b\otimes b$ to itself, and consequently is the identity under the twist-additivity identification. For blocks of sizes $d,e$, interchange sends $b^{\otimes d}\otimes b^{\otimes e}$ to $b^{\otimes e}\otimes b^{\otimes d}$; both identify with $b^{\otimes(d+e)}$, and the shift sign is $(-1)^{(-2d)(-2e)}=+1$. It follows from Step 7 that each adjacent coordinate transposition preserves $I_m$, and hence that every coordinate permutation does. By the projection-formula compatibility in [lem-sf-kunneth-coherence] and Step 6 it preserves $\tau_{m,K}$ for every $K$, without moving $K$ past a shifted coordinate factor. Finally the exceptional Hom bijection of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class] is injective and natural, so equality of these transposes proves equality of the two transported comparisons. Combined with Step 4 this gives the asserted composition law and equality for the two block orderings.
